slot.brief: Give rate constants at two temperatures and ask for activation energy plus the temperature at which the rate doubles — requires logarithmic manipulation of the two-point Arrhenius form.

stem: A first-order reaction has $k=1.0\times10^{-3}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ at $600\ \text{K}$ and $k=8.0\times10^{-3}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ at $900\ \text{K}$. Find $E_a$ and the temperature at which $k$ doubles from its value at $600\ \text{K}$. Take $R=8.314\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Using the Arrhenius relation, ln(8) = (Ea/R)(1/600 − 1/900), giving Ea ≈ 31.1 kJ mol⁻¹. For doubling from 600 K, ln(2) = (Ea/R)(1/600 − 1/T), giving T ≈ 675 K.

working:
$\ln 8=\dfrac{E_a}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{600}-\dfrac{1}{900}\right)$, so $E_a=1800R\ln 8=31.1\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. $\ln 2=\dfrac{E_a}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{600}-\dfrac{1}{T}\right)$; hence $\dfrac{1}{T}=\dfrac{1}{600}-\dfrac{1}{5400}=\dfrac{1}{675}$ and $T=675\ \text{K}$.

Independent check: Using the Arrhenius relation, ln(8) = (Ea/R)(1/600 − 1/900), giving Ea ≈ 31.1 kJ mol⁻¹. For doubling from 600 K, ln(2) = (Ea/R)(1/600 − 1/T), giving T ≈ 675 K.
solution:
Using the Arrhenius equation, $\ln(k_2/k_1)=\dfrac{E_a}{R}(1/T_1-1/T_2)$,
$$E_a=\dfrac{R\ln 8}{1/600-1/900}=1800R\ln 8=31.1\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}.$$
For doubling from $600\ \text{K}$, $\ln 2=\dfrac{E_a}{R}(1/600-1/T)$, giving $T=675\ \text{K}$. (C)
